Comparison: On this evidence, a direct like-for-like comparison of Edward Jones's disclosures and initiatives for younger investors against those of competitors is not valid. Edward Jones discloses qualitative initiatives (a digital platform for Next Generation investors, Financial Planning Services, a Quicken minority stake) but no younger-investor growth metrics, whereas Schwab discloses both specific initiatives (Schwab Starter Kit, Teen Investor Account, no/low commissions, 35 hours weekly of live content) and quantified younger-investor growth figures (e.g., ~70% of new-to-firm retail households being Gen Z and millennials, 61% of new clients Gen Z/Millennial). The two firms' young-investor growth figures rest on unverified metric definitions, so those figures cannot be compared across firms; and Morgan Stanley and Raymond James Financial produce no such disclosures in the documents searched, while Merrill's disclosures concern its own under-40 financial advisors rather than younger clients.
